bounded_finding_titles.M2-B50: the cgroup identity check protected only the final removal, so a same-named replacement could already be enumerated, killed and signalled
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B51: terminal cleanup was derived from cgroup absence, so a killed child that was never reaped, a late joiner and an unexplained ECHILD all read as finished
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B52: capacity was checked and not held, insertion was unconditional, nothing was locked, and a registrar exception silently destroyed the only handle
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B53: reference release and cleanup handles were unprotected check-then-set, so two callers could spend one linear capability twice
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B54: a registry drain with no caller deadline created a fresh budget inside the loop, so a bounded drain at capacity could spend sixty-four complete budgets
bounded_finding_titles.M2-M55: the committed current artifacts carried two different current M2 totals: 761/43 in one section and 749/42 in another

known_limitations: The delegated physical qualification of this revision was performed by the operator rather than by this agent, which has no interactive sudo here; the transcript is recorded verbatim and its exact totals are the ones the current artifacts carry.

Exactness of the final rmdir is proved by verifying the owned identity immediately before it and by asking the retained descriptor afterwards whether the owned object is the object that went away; Linux offers no rmdir-by-descriptor, so this verify-then-act-then-prove sequence is the strongest available construction and its post-condition is recorded rather than assumed.
A member of the domain is proved to be this controller's child from /proc/<pid>/status; on a host without procfs no member is adopted, and the obligation is left standing rather than guessed at.
Independent acceptance and installed-path qualification are not claimed.

requirement_dispositions.note: Descriptor-bound exact cgroup identity before every read that informs a destructive action and before every destructive action; owned-process reap as a separate terminal obligation; atomic hard-bounded fail-closed registry retention; serialised linear release and cleanup; one global drain deadline.

The cleanup document now separates containment from process lifecycle, names every identity refusal with its operation, reports registration failures as typed lifecycle failures, and carries the one-deadline drain ledger.  Deferred retry accounting remains Milestone 3 work and is not closed here.
